translations.source_sense_description: Kartenspiel: Spielkarte von besonderem Wert, kann andere Karten ersetzen

glosses: A person who makes jokes.
A funny person.
A jester.
A playing card that features a picture of a joker (that is, a jester) and that may be used as a wild card in some card games.
Something kept in reserve that can be used to gain an advantage; a trump card.

examples.text: Rebus decided to use their joker. 'Mr Lintz made a phone call to this office. He was talking for over twenty minutes.'
Tash Wilson played her 'joker' , pulling her chair so close our legs were almost touching. 'Hey, Chris, do you want to go out sometime? All you've got to do is say the word.'

The director made me understand that my bubble of stardom could burst just as soon as it had been inflated if I didn't watch my attitude. Then he used his joker. I had an understudy so if I messed up or tried to create a scene, I would be summarily replaced.

glosses: An unspecified, vaguely disreputable person.

examples.text: Some joker keeps throwing eggs at my windows.

glosses: An unspecified, vaguely disreputable person.
A loser.

examples.text: Don't waste your breath on these jokers round here.

glosses: A man.
A clause in a contract that undermines its apparent provisions.

examples.text: Discussion of contracts and the many provisions contained therein led to a vote making it the sense of the convention that manufacturers should use a simple sales contract, free from jokers.
Then, sir, on page 12 of the agreement there is a joker clause, which provides for payments in addition to the ten per cent, […]
Stone claimed that there was a Joker in the contract, one clause (No. 2) calling for two weeks' notice and another (No. 8) calling for payment on a par-day basis after the first two weeks.
The object of these provisions is to prevent insertion of "jokers" or "sleepers" in bills and securing passage under the false color of the title.

glosses: A friendly unit that acts as a suspected hostile unit in a military excercise.

examples.text: Joker - A friendly track or contact acting as a "suspect" track for exercise purposes only. (STANAG 1241)

glosses: The option, in a pub quiz, of selecting one particular round in which one's team will score double points.

examples.text: We used our joker as soon as the topic of sports was announced, since we are sport experts.

glosses: A fairy chess piece that moves like the last piece that was moved by the opponent.

examples.text: The problem is that it would be difficult to use a joker offensively since you could never know how it was going to move, meaning it’d be most useful setting it up for potential queen/rook captures to disincentivize your opponent from moving those pieces.

translations.source_sense_description: Kartenspiel: Spielkarte von besonderem Wert, kann andere Karten ersetzen

glosses: Carte qui peut prendre à certains jeux n’importe quelle valeur, selon la volonté de celui qui la détient.

examples.text: Ainsi du joker dans le jeu de cartes ou de l'avantage d'une pièce dans le jeu des échecs pour rétablir l'équilibre entre deux joueurs d'inégale force.

glosses: Lettre blanche à laquelle on peut désigner l’identité de n’importe quelle lettre.
Avantage quelconque que l’on emploie si besoin est.

examples.text: Avancer un joker, donner son joker, refuser de répondre à une question.
Sortir son joker, se sortir d’une situation embarrassante par un moyen inattendu.

glosses: Métacaractère passe-partout, utilisé pour désigner un caractère quelconque, comme le point dans /file.*/ dans les expressions rationnelles, ou un ou plusieurs caractères quelconques, comme l’astérisque dans *.txt sur un shell.

examples.text: Dans le cadre d’une recherche par mots-clés également, les troncatures sont des signes permettant de remplacer un ou plusieurs caractères d’un mot par un astérisque ou par une lettre « joker ».

glosses: (Audiovisuel) Personne choisie pour en remplacer une autre.

examples.text: Après avoir fait ses armes pendant neuf ans à LCI, il devient joker à la présentation des journaux du week-end de TF1 durant l'été 2006.

glosses: Plaisanter, blaguer.

examples.text: Tu jokes, là ?
